lead_time_analysis.stability: Unstable — bimodal distribution with fast (~0.6d) and slow (~2.8d) delivery modes

narrative: Material PL3__M9B8DDA7 exhibits smooth, high-volume daily demand (~3,310 units/day) with moderate variability (CV=0.262) and no detectable trend across the observed period. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.730) due to a bimodal delivery pattern, with transport uncertainty accounting for 77% of lead-time variance. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and orders at MOQ (700 units), resulting in ~1,186 orders/year and dominantly ordering-driven costs. The recommended (r,Q) policy introduces a 4,833-unit safety stock and 2,199-unit order quantity — the latter being constrained by the 7,033-unit storage capacity limit — reducing total annual costs by 62% while achieving the 95% service level target.
warnings: Storage capacity is binding: unconstrained EOQ=8695 reduced to 2199 to satisfy max_storage_units=7032.989 with safety_stock=4833.
Capacity utilization at 99.99% — any demand spike during replenishment cycle risks exceeding storage limit.
3 demand outliers detected and winsorised at upper bound 5136.966 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and near-continuous (77.8% non-zero days, CV=0.262) making a continuous-review policy appropriate. The (r,Q) model provides tight service-level control by triggering a fixed replenishment whenever stock falls to the reorder point, which is efficient for this high-throughput, stable-demand material.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (7,033 units) is fully binding at the recommended policy (SS=4,833 + Q=2,199 = 7,032 units, 99.99% utilization). The unconstrained EOQ of 8,695 units cannot be implemented. This cap increases annual ordering frequency (378 vs optimal ~135 orders/year at full EOQ), adding approximately $17,850/year in excess ordering costs. Capacity expansion would unlock further savings.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility (MOQ 700 + SS 4833 = 5533 < 7033). However, capacity expansion is strongly recommended: current storage prevents full EOQ implementation and leaves zero buffer for demand spikes post-replenishment.
